issue.title: sase-telegram receiver-runtime generation-digest tests see equal digests after file replacement
issue.description:
In the linked sase-telegram repo, two receiver-runtime generation-digest tests sometimes
see equal digests after the test replaces the files the digest covers. Reported by
phase sase-11y.10.1.1 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #2, 2026-09-20) while verifying the
telegram-rearm change in sase-telegram. The failure also happened on an unchanged tree,
so the rearm change did not cause it.

- Tests: `tests/test_receiver_runtime.py::test_host_plugin_and_native_changes_each_new_generation`
  and `tests/test_receiver_runtime.py::test_executable_replacement_changes_generation`
  (sase-telegram repo).
- Observed: plugin pytest run of 654 passed with 1 digest test failed; the failure
  recurred on an unchanged tree.
- Suspected root cause (unconfirmed): the generation digest keys on file mtime/size.
  When a test rewrites a file within the filesystem's mtime granularity with the same
  size, the digest does not change.

task_type_fields.evidence: Proposed by sase-11y.10.1.1 note #2 (2026-09-20). One of the two generation-digest tests (this one or test_host_plugin_and_native_changes_each_new_generation) failed in a 654-test plugin run, and the failure also happened on an unchanged tree. The fail rate was not measured. Suspected cause: mtime granularity.

evidence.note: Independent reproduction by the sase-11y.11 land agent in the sase-telegram linked checkout at f99521c (venv with local sase 0.17.1 / sase-core-rs 0.34.70). just check: 653 passed, 2 failed, and both failures are the generation-digest tests. Running .venv/bin/pytest tests/test_receiver_runtime.py fails at file level (2 failed/7 passed; after git stash on a pristine tree, 1 failed/8 passed). test_executable_replacement_changes_generation passes when run alone. The failing assertion is replaced.digest != baseline.digest after _write_executable rewrites same-size content ('exit 0' -> 'exit 1'). That fits the mtime-granularity hypothesis: size is unchanged and the rewrite lands in the same mtime tick. Fix direction: bump mtime explicitly (os.utime with +1s ns) in the test helper. Also reported by phase sase-11y.11.5 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #1).

Relayed by sase-16n.land from PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP sase-16n.9#1: while landing the telegram project-tag change (aff9a23), the sase-16n.9 phase agent saw tests/test_receiver_runtime.py::test_host_plugin_and_native_changes_each_new_generation fail in the full sase-telegram suite (673 passed otherwise) and fail again with its changes stashed on a clean tree, i.e. the same receiver generation-fingerprint digest failure.

Independent reproduction during sase_tg_inbound split verification (2026-09-23): full sase-telegram suite showed 676 passed/1 failed, then official check showed 675 passed/2 failed, both failures in tests/test_receiver_runtime.py (test_host_plugin_and_native_changes_each_new_generation, test_executable_replacement_changes_generation) with identical digests after same-size rewrites. Stashed all split changes (git stash -u) and re-ran tests/test_receiver_runtime.py 4x on the pristine tree: 1-2 failures each run in the same two tests. Unrelated to the split; same mtime-granularity root cause suspected in the bead.

payload.description: Need the candidate flake report before corroborating

evidence.note: Relayed by the sase-17m land agent from PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP sase-17m.7 note #1 (2026-09-25): while verifying the telegram /show agent-session cutover (5daae9d), the sase-17m.7 phase agent saw test_host_plugin_and_native_changes_each_new_generation and test_executable_replacement_changes_generation fail intermittently on clean HEAD in the full sase-telegram suite (678 passed otherwise). It identified the same root cause: the digest hashes path+size+mtime_ns rather than content, so same-size rewrites collide.
